patch_description:
The current program achieves 0.91 combined score with only 3 unique parameters (ry_basis, cry_nnn, rz_readout) per block, resulting in 20 total parameters. Prior high-performing candidates (0.93 test accuracy) used 4 unique parameters per block (26 total), with richer entanglement structures including both nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor CRY gates.

The current ANSATZ_SPEC is too compact. It has:
- Layer 1: RY (shared across all qubits)
- Layer 2: Fixed CZ ring
- Layer 3: CRY ring (shared parameter)
- Layer 4: RZ (shared across all qubits)

This lacks the depth and expressivity of prior successful designs. The improvement adds:
1. An additional parametrized layer of next-nearest-neighbor CRY gates (reusing the cry_nnn parameter for efficiency, similar to prior designs)
2. This increases expressivity without adding new unique parameters, leveraging the same cry_nnn parameter across both nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor connectivity

This mirrors the structure of the second prior program which had both nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor CRY layers sharing the same parameter, achieving 0.93 test accuracy with 26 parameters and 196 depth.
